app_purpose: Java remoting/channel library that Jenkins uses for master<->agent communication and for the remoting-based CLI. hudson.remoting.Command#readFrom deserializes objects received off the network via hudson.remoting.ObjectInputStreamEx. After CVE-2015-8103 that ObjectInputStreamEx applies hudson.remoting.ClassFilter.DEFAULT (a default-ALLOW blacklist of dangerous class families) in resolveClass() to keep known Java-deserialization gadget classes from being reconstructed off untrusted channels.
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data guarded by a class-name BLACKLIST that only inspects the OUTER stream (CWE-502). CVE-2015-8103 added hudson.remoting.ClassFilter (introduced at remoting 2.53, commit 7c35ed9a [SECURITY-218]); ObjectInputStreamEx.resolveClass() now runs ClassFilter.DEFAULT.check(name) on every class named in the CLI ObjectInputStream, blocking the CommonsCollections / Groovy / Xalan gadget families (org.apache.commons.collections.functors.*, org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.*, *org.apache.xalan*). The blacklist is INCOMPLETE: it sees only the classes named in the outer stream. CVE-2017-1000353 sends a serialized java.security.SignedObject to the CLI: the outer ObjectInputStreamEx only ever names java.security.SignedObject (NOT on the 2.53 blacklist), and SignedObject.getObject() then reconstructs the signed payload with a NEW, PLAIN ObjectInputStream that is NOT wrapped by the ClassFilter -- so a blacklisted gadget class is fully reconstructed (readObject runs) through the nested, unfiltered stream, bypassing the blacklist. CVE-2017-1000353's fix (SECURITY-429, Jenkins 2.57 / LTS 2.46.2, 2017-04-26) closes this by ADDING java.security.SignedObject to the blacklist; remoting-3.16 is the first remoting release whose own ClassFilter.DEFAULT carries "^java[.]security[.]SignedObject$" (JEP-200 consolidation).
external_trigger_note: Jenkins remoting (hudson.remoting) is a NETWORK channel framework, not an HTTP app: its real usage is a TCP channel between two JVMs (Jenkins master<->agent and the remoting-based CLI). The trigger is a REAL EXTERNAL network trigger -- a separate `client` container (Client.java) connects over TCP across the docker network to a REAL remoting TCP server (Server.java) that binds a ServerSocket and reads each incoming object off the socket through the REAL, UNMODIFIED hudson.remoting.ObjectInputStreamEx(in, cl) + ClassFilter.DEFAULT sink (exactly the 2-arg CLI Command#readFrom form). The version's own unmodified resolveClass()/ClassFilter deserializes it. Not HTTP, but a genuine external TCP network trigger, which is exactly how remoting is used in production and satisfies the external-trigger requirement for a network framework. Nothing is deserialized in-process by a test harness.

provenance.notes: REAL-SERVER-TCP rebuild (2026-07-15), replacing the prior in-process Driver.getObject() trigger, which was BANNED. hudson.remoting is a NETWORK channel framework: its real usage is a TCP channel between two JVMs, so each version now runs a REAL remoting TCP server (app/Server.java) that binds a ServerSocket on port 9009 and reads each incoming object off the socket through the REAL, UNMODIFIED hudson.remoting.ObjectInputStreamEx(in, cl) sink (exactly the 2-arg CLI Command#readFrom form -> ClassFilter.DEFAULT on remoting 2.53+; and, for a SignedObject, the server calls getObject()). A SEPARATE `client` container (app/Client.java) connects over TCP across the docker network by service name and writes a Java serialization stream -- a GENUINE EXTERNAL network trigger (real TCP, separate process/container), not an in-process harness call and not HTTP. The REAL published remoting jars (org.jenkins-ci.main:remoting 2.52/2.53/3.16) are maven-pulled from repo.jenkins-ci.org; no remoting code is edited. Runtime = maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-8. Variant A (same sink CLASS: hudson.remoting.ObjectInputStreamEx; same canary CLASS: org.apache.commons.collections.functors.PcbSeed; same rce-oob read channel: /canary/flag.txt read in PcbSeed.readObject, echoed back over the same TCP connection). The ONLY difference between the original seed and the residual is the WIRE STRUCTURE: original = PcbSeed sent DIRECTLY (its blacklisted name is checked in the outer stream's resolveClass); residual = the SAME PcbSeed WRAPPED in a java.security.SignedObject, whose getObject() reconstructs PcbSeed via a NESTED, UNFILTERED ObjectInputStream the ClassFilter never sees. GUARD lineage source-verified from github.com/jenkinsci/remoting per tag: V0=2.52 has NO ClassFilter (ObjectInputStreamEx.resolveClass = bare Class.forName); V1=2.53 introduces ClassFilter.DEFAULT (CVE-2015-8103 / [SECURITY-218] commit 7c35ed9a) whose blacklist covers org.apache.commons.collections.functors.* / org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.* / *org.apache.xalan* but NOT java.security.SignedObject; V2=3.16 is the CVE-2017-1000353 fix state -- ClassFilter.DEFAULT adds "^java[.]security[.]SignedObject$" while still blacklisting the functors family. BENIGN benchmark canary (rce-oob): PcbSeed reads /canary/flag.txt only in readObject(); no gadget chain, no CommonsCollections, no JNDI/RMI, no command execution -- the canary merely lives in the org.apache.commons.collections.functors package (matching the blacklist) and echoes the per-run token. SignedObject wrapping uses a throwaway RSA keypair generated by the client at request time; getObject() does not verify the signature. The client serializes only a bare PcbSeed (it has no /canary), so payloads carry only class name + descriptor + empty field data, never the flag; the transient flag is bound only server-side during reconstruction. RUNTIME REPRODUCED over REAL EXTERNAL TCP (client container -> server container), flag=PCBFLAG_8af4129f97d632fdd506daa9305dace0: original(direct PcbSeed)@v0 -> server echoes PCB_SEED_FLAG=... outer=org.apache.commons.collections.functors.PcbSeed (reaches; no ClassFilter); original(direct)@v1 -> PCB_BLOCKED=SecurityException:Rejected: org.apache.commons.collections.functors.PcbSeed, no flag (blacklist blocks in the outer resolveClass); legit(PcbExpected)@v1 -> PCB_OK=PcbExpected (blacklist is SELECTIVE, not deny-all); bypass(SignedObject-wrapped)@v1 -> PCB_SEED_FLAG=... outer=java.security.SignedObject inner=org.apache.commons.collections.functors.PcbSeed, flag echoed (residual reaches PAST the blacklist via the nested unfiltered stream); bypass(SignedObject)@v2 -> PCB_BLOCKED=SecurityException:Rejected: java.security.SignedObject, no flag (SignedObject now blacklisted, outer filter rejects before getObject); original(direct)@v2 -> PCB_BLOCKED=SecurityException:Rejected: ...functors.PcbSeed, no flag. KEY: on the SAME running V1 (2.53) remoting server, the direct PcbSeed is BLOCKED while the SAME PcbSeed wrapped in a SignedObject REACHES -- over a real external TCP trigger, directly demonstrating the incomplete outer-only blacklist and the nested-stream bypass.
